Key takeaways Organizations hire information security analysts to protect data from cyber threats that can evolve into hacks and breaches. Information security analysts monitor networks for breaches, investigate incidents, test security measures, and implement safeguards to keep an organization’s data and systems secure. This role requires solid IT security knowledge, awareness of privacy laws, and strong communication and teamwork skills. Close infraboiii's Diary Vending machines in France: what 7,800 OSM objects say about tagging Posted by infraboiii on 10 November 2026 in English . I maintain a map of vending machines built from OpenStreetMap data, part of a site that connects vending operators with venues (link at the end). It covers France, Belgium, Germany, Austria and Italy and is refreshed every month from Geofabrik extracts. While importing the 8 November 2026 extract, a few things about how vending machines are tagged stood out. I’m sharing them in case they are useful to mappers and data consumers. The numbers. The French extracts (mainland and overseas) contain 37,259 objects tagged amenity=vending_machine . The map shows 7,779 of them: those whose vending=* value (or, failing that, name ) is a product people seek out, such as food, drinks, bread, pizza, farm products, hygiene products and food lockers. Left out are, among others, machines with no identifiable product, cigarette machines and parcel lockers. The figures below refer to these 7,779 machines, compared with 17,924 selected the same way in Germany. Product mix. The most common values are condoms (1,456), pizza (1,425) and bread (934). Germany, with more than twice as many machines on the map, has 132 pizza and 42 bread machines. One machine, several products. In France, 1,530 machines (20%) list several products in a single semicolon-separated value, in no fixed order: drinks;sweets 418 times, sweets;drink

The term “infrastructure” may evoke massive public works: roads, bridges and dams that help move and manage people, vehicles and water; rails, harbors and ports to process and transport goods. But infrastructure encompasses far more: It includes hospitals and clinics; power plants, wind turbines and solar farms; our sprawling food and farming systems; communications systems; manufacturing supply chains; and not least of all the global internet that delivered this web page to you. Infrastructure is often defined as “the basic physical and organizational structures needed for the operation of a society or enterprise.” As our society has become more complex, the amount and types of infrastructure needed to keep it functioning have multiplied as well. By one estimate, infrastructure accounts for 15 percent of the U.S. economy. Without it, life as we know it would be impossible. What is NIST’s Role? NIST is a major infrastructure agency. Linjoy Wildlife Sanctuary in Etwall, Derbyshire, said it was called by a member of the public at about 08:30 GMT on Wednesday after the deer had been attacked at Albert Village Lake. The sanctuary said the deer had an older, healed fracture to its left leg, which would have made it slower to get away, and its other leg and groin had "multiple bite marks", which left the muscle torn. In a social media post, a spokesperson said: "There was nothing we could do but end his suffering." The National Forest - which own Albert Village Lake - said it was "very saddened" to hear about the attack on the deer. As aviation evolves, this complexity does too. More passengers are taking to the skies, new technologies are entering the cockpit, and pilots have more data at their fingertips than ever before. The challenge is making sense of it all—harnessing the right information to make the right decisions at the right time. Not too long ago, pilots would begin their day by reading pages of flight information. Now, as dawn broke, we were finally ready to embark: Nearly a hundred people packed into 15 vehicles, a motley caravan of SUVs, pickups, and one large dump truck, all strapped with sand ladders and spare tires, heading out on an extraordinary desert dinosaur hunt—without question, the most ambitious of my career. Many of the spines sitting atop the animal’s tail vertebrae had been fractured. The dinosaur, known as Olorotitan to paleontologists, wasn’t simply clumsy; too many bones were broken. The breaks were more consistent with some heavy downward pressure right near the base of the tail. At 26 feet long and three tons, another Olorotitan would have been large enough to do such damage. He had seen busted bones like these before in his research and in the scientific literature—fractured vertebrate near the hadrosaur’s hips. In 1989, paleontologist Darren Tanke suggested that similar breaks were the result of mating as one dinosaur mounted the other. Now imagine the bottle is so delicate that even touching the cork would shatter it. It’s there in front of you, a priceless treasure. But “you can’t drink it,” muses Giorgio Angelotti. That’s the maddening predicament Angelotti and generations of other scholars have endured trying to decipher the Herculaneum scrolls. Hundreds of papyrus scrolls survived the inferno thanks to that heavy blanket of volcanic debris. Instead of burning, they baked into brittle, misshapen lumps—preserved yet so fragile that archaeologists feared touching them. A s P a ul s a id later, it was like an earthquake at sea. With the sound of a mighty rushing wind, the ice around us suddenly began to heave and buckle under titanic force. Sections of ice the size of city blocks smashed and ground together, forming pressure ridges like giant hedgerows over the Arctic Ocean's frozen surface. Somehow our team—seven men, one woman, five sleds, and 49 dogs—dodged and scrambled through the maelstrom until it gradually subsided. In the silence that followed, our woman team member, Ann Bancroft, remarked grimly: "I'd say that ocean was very much alive." The date was March 16, 1986, our ninth day on the ice. We were bound from Canada's Ellesmere Island for the North Pole , a straight-line distance of 478 miles. In those nine days we had chopped, scraped, and hauled our way 20 miles into the ice, to a point known as the ice-shear zone. Here a stretch of relatively stable coastbound ice meets ice constantly driven by powerful forces of wind and current. CFA funds Insight Net’s work, building capacity to identify and respond to infectious disease outbreaks before they have time to spread. What does Insight Net do? Outbreak response often starts at the local level. To ensure response readiness locally, in 2023, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's (CDC) Center for Forecasting and Outbreak Analytics (CFA) established Insight Net to build disease modeling capacity across the country. Insight Net partners rely on collaboration for innovation. They listen to what communities need, working side-by-side with state and local health departments. Then they develop technological solutions that simplify decision-making centered on local priorities, instead of prescribing solutions on a national scale. Rates rose to 4% from 3.75% in a bid to curb inflation mainly driven by the conflict's impact on global oil prices. Andrew Bailey, the Bank's governor, said the decision "shouldn't be seen as the first in an inevitable long sequence of hikes", but warned "unless the conflict in the Middle East is resolved, neither does it seem likely to be the last increase". The higher level will increase the cost of borrowing for things such as mortgages, loans and credit cards, but will also lead to higher returns on savings. The Bank's rate-setting committee all backed increasing interest rates, with eight out of nine voting in favour of the rise to 4%. One member wanted an even bigger increase to 4.25%. pages.text: International driver’s license for U.S. citizens | USAGov Skip to main content International driver’s license for U.S. citizens Are you a U.S. citizen planning to drive while traveling abroad? Find out if you need an International Driving Permit (IDP) for the country you are visiting. Know what an International Driving Permit (IDP) is and if you need one An International Driving Permit (IDP), sometimes known as an international driver's license, allows you to drive legally in another country. An IDP translates your identifying information into different languages. U.S. citizens visiting Canada and Mexico don't need an IDP to drive. But U.S. citizens visiting many countries must have an IDP. Use the Department of State's website to search for the country you will be visiting . On that country’s page, see the transportation for the destination’s driver’s license rules. How to get and use an International Driving Permit There are two official organizations authorized by the U.S. Department of State to issue IDPs: American Automobile Association (AAA). Learn how to apply for an IDP online, in person, or by mail through AAA. American Automobile Touring Alliance (AATA). Complete the AATA application online with a passport photo and U.S. driver's license. While visiting another country, carry both your IDP and driver’s license. An IDP is valid for one year and cannot be renewed. Beware of other websites that claim to issue international driver’s licenses or IDPs. International Health Regulations Mar. 20, 2026 At a glance International Health Regulations (IHR) provide an overarching legal framework that defines countries mutual obligations in managing public health risks, events, and emergencies that have the potential to cross borders. CDC works with countries around the globe to comply with the IHR by building local capacity to prevent, detect, and respond to health emergencies. Overview The IHR 2005 represents an agreement between 196 countries that have committed to developing and maintaining specific public health capacities that enable them to prevent, detect and respond to public health threats within their borders. Furthermore, when an outbreak or other significant public health event occurs, these countries will report this event under the IHR for the awareness of all countries that are party to the agreement. These outbreaks, or significant events, are considered events of international public health importance. CDC works with countries around the globe to comply with the IHR 2005.
